subject.title: fix(agents): keep finite LLM idle watchdog under unlimited run budgets

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this Track B3 timeout contract after the finite self-hosted cap bug is fixed: config timeoutSeconds: 0 means unlimited run budget, unlimited budgets keep finite provider-class liveness watchdogs, and self-hosted implicit idle defaults are 300s?
rationale: The code repair is mechanical, but changing an existing config validation contract and implicit provider-default behavior can affect existing operators after upgrade.

options.title: Accept Track B3 After Cap Fix
options.body: Repair the self-hosted cap ordering, keep config-zero and 300s self-hosted semantics, and proceed after normal draft and CI review.

options.title: Narrow The Config Contract
options.body: Keep the idle-watchdog sentinel repair but defer or remove config-file timeoutSeconds: 0 acceptance until a broader config migration decision.

options.title: Hold For Lifecycle Umbrella
options.body: Keep this draft paused until the broader run-lifecycle design settles liveness thresholds and recovery policy together.

recommendation.title: Accept Track B3 After Cap Fix
recommendation.body: Repair the self-hosted cap ordering, keep config-zero and 300s self-hosted semantics, and proceed after normal draft and CI review.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the Track B3 proposal and have prior idle-timeout landing history, making them the clearest routing owner for the semantics decision packet.
